claims.text: An actively trained machine-learned interatomic potential based on representative ab initio solid and liquid configurations will mimic the ab initio phase space of multicomponent HEAs better than traditional EAM references.
The proposed intervention applies to multicomponent high-entropy alloys in near-melting solid and high-temperature liquid states.
Neural-network or moment-tensor potentials can be trained on diverse ab initio configurations from both solid and liquid phases for use as thermodynamic-integration references.
The proposed method is applicable from approximately Tm - 100 K to Tm + 20 K.
The proposed method is applicable to typical multiple-principal-element HEA compositions exhibiting non-ideal mixing and large configurational spaces.
A machine-learned potential can interpolate among diverse local atomic environments.
Interpolation among diverse local environments enhances overlap between the reference ensemble and the ab initio target ensemble.
Training on extensive samples of local configurations from both phases reduces structural discrepancies between the reference potential and the ab initio system.
Reduced structural discrepancies prevent thermodynamic integration from traversing poorly represented regions of configuration space.
Improved configurational sampling reduces mismatch between the reference and target free-energy landscapes.
The machine-learned reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path-mismatch errors by approximately 50% relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
Reducing thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will produce more reliable free-energy estimates.
TOR-TILD EAM reference potentials have limited phase-space overlap with the ab initio target, especially for complex liquids.
Extreme local distortions in compositionally complex HEAs may exceed the representational capacity of the machine-learned potential.
Sparse ab initio training data may limit the performance of the proposed reference potential.
Performance may deteriorate for compositions that deviate substantially from typical refractory HEAs.
Preliminary comparisons in elemental or binary systems indicate that machine-learned potentials improve accuracy.
The magnitude and universality of the integration-error reduction across HEA compositions and near-melting conditions have not been established.

The hypothesis is falsified if the machine-learned reference fails to achieve at least a 50% reduction in integration path-mismatch error relative to EAM across statistically robust tests spanning multiple HEA compositions and temperatures.
